mappings.note: Both are title verses (To the choirmaster; of David). 'Shoshannim' matches 'Liljer'.
Both contain: Save me, God, for waters have reached my soul/life.
Both describe sinking in deep mire/water and being swept away.
Both describe exhaustion from crying, hoarse throat, and eyes failing while waiting for God.

Translation v5 combines the first half of OSMAIN v5 (haters without cause) with a phrase 'those who attack me... strengthen themselves' which is not in OSMAIN v5. The second part of OSMAIN v5 ('Mektige er de som vil utrydde meg...') is missing from Translation v5 and appears to be omitted or merged elsewhere, but the translation text provided for v5 does not fully match the full content of OSMAIN v5.
Both: God knows my folly, sins not hidden.
Both: Do not let those who hope in you be shamed because of me...
Both: For your sake I bear reproach, shame covers my face.
Both: Stranger to brothers, unknown to mother's sons.
Both: Zeal for your house has consumed me...
Both: I wept and fasted, but it became reproach.
Both: Clothed in sackcloth, object of mockery.
Both: Those at the gate speak of me, drunkards sing songs about me.
Both: Prayer to you in time of favor; answer with great mercy/fidelity.
Both: Draw me from mire, deliver from enemies and deep waters.
Both: Let not flood overwhelm, let not pit swallow, let not well close mouth.
Both: Answer me, Lord, for your grace is good; turn to me in mercy.
Both: Do not hide face, I am in distress; hurry and answer.
Both: Come near to my soul, redeem it; deliver me for enemies' sake.
Both: You know my reproach, shame, humiliation; adversaries before you.
Both: Reproach broke heart, despair; waited for compassion/comforters but found none.
Both: Galle in food, vinegar for thirst.
Both: Let their table be a snare/trap.
Both: Darken eyes so they don't see; make loins/hips tremble.
Both: Pour out wrath/burning anger upon them.
Both: Let their dwelling be desolate; no one live in tents.
Both: They persecute the one you struck; add pain to those you wounded.
Both: Add guilt to their guilt; let them not share in righteousness.
Both: Blotted out of book of life; not written with the righteous.

Translation v30 matches OSMAIN v30 ('I am afflicted... let your salvation lift me up'). However, the translation phrase 'me mettra dans une haute retraite' (will put me in a high retreat) is a slight interpretative variation of 'løfte meg opp' (lift me up), but content is effectively the same. No extra text.
Both: Praise God's name with song and thanksgiving.
Both: Pleasing to Lord more than an ox/calf with horns and hooves.
Both: The humble see and rejoice; let hearts of those seeking God live.
Both: Lord hears the poor/afflicted and does not despise captives.
Both: Heaven and earth praise Him; seas and everything in them.

Translation v36 matches the first half of OSMAIN v36 ('God will save Sion and build cities...'). It stops before the final clause 'De skal bo der og ta landet i eie' (They shall dwell there and take possession of it), though the translation says 'on y habitera, on la possédera' which covers that. Wait, looking closely: OSMAIN v36 ends with 'ta landet i eie'. Translation v36 ends with 'on la possédera'. This is an exact match.

This verse exists in the translation but has no corresponding text in the provided OSMAIN text (which ends at v36). The content 'La race de ses serviteurs l'aura pour héritage; ceux qui aiment son nom, y auront leur demeure.' is an addition found in some Hebrew manuscripts or other traditions (like the Masoretic Text's final verse of Psalm 69) but is missing from this specific OSMAIN version.

extraContent.description: Complete verse not found in OSMAIN. Content: 'La race de ses serviteurs l'aura pour héritage; ceux qui aiment son nom, y auront leur demeure.' (The seed of his servants shall inherit it; those who love his name shall dwell therein.)
